title: Pilot: graceful degradation & function-calling check-in
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on function-calling behaviors, structured output reliability under streaming, and graceful fallback policies. Customer ran pilot traffic, saw two failure modes: truncated streaming outputs breaking schema validation, and rare API 503s causing tool-calls to retry incorrectly. Agreed next steps: provide SDK patch for deterministic function-call retries, share a small validation harness, run a short canary with fallback model pinned, and share security/SSO docs. Action items and owners captured.
topics: SDK hooks for local schema validation

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (Northridge), Marcus Lee (Northridge), Samira Khan (Northridge PM), Evan Roberts (Northridge Security), Olivia Chen (Northridge SWE)

[00:00] Jordan Miller: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we've got 50 minutes. Quick agenda: run through the pilot results you shared, dig into the two edge failure modes you flagged, go over the SDK patch and a proposed canary, then Q&A. Sound good?
[00:09] Alicia Gomez: Yep, sounds good. We've got some logs and a repro for the streaming truncation.
[00:14] Marcus Lee: And the 503s seemed correlated with a backend pool shift, so interested in fallbacks.
[00:19] Priya Kapoor: Cool. Before we jump in, quick context — our goal is to make sure function-calls are "at-least-once" in a deterministic way for your orchestration, and that streaming partials don't break the structured output validation.
[00:28] Samira Khan: Right, our product needs reliable tool invocation semantics, otherwise downstream reconciliation logic fails.
[00:33] Jordan Miller: Alicia, can you summarize what you saw in the pilot traffic?
[00:38] Alicia Gomez: Sure. So in the 72 hour pilot we sent about ~240k tokens, most flows are fine. Two categories of failures: one, streaming responses were cut mid-object during network jitter and our JSON schema validator choked. Two, roughly 0.03% of requests returned a transient 503; our client retried but that caused duplicate tool invocations because our retry semantics are currently tied to status-level heuristics, not function-call acknowledgements.
[01:08] Olivia Chen: To add, sometimes the streaming chunk contained an extra comma or broken escape and the SDK's parser threw and didn't attempt to re-request the missing tail.
[01:17] Priya Kapoor: Ok, so parsing/truncation on partial streams and idempotency of function-calls on retries. Two different problems but related to how the SDK exposes hooks.
[01:26] Marcus Lee: Do you have a recommended approach for idempotent tool-calls? We can't risk double charges or double payouts to vendors in our flows.
[01:33] Priya Kapoor: Absolutely. The approach we proposed in the last doc is to use an idempotency token tied to your orchestration ID, and for us to provide a deterministic retry layer in the SDK that will only re-issue the function-call if we haven't previously received a confirmed callback. But important: if streaming breaks before the server-side function-call commit is confirmed, the client needs a way to reconcile — re-run with same idempotency token or call a status endpoint.
[01:55] Jordan Miller: We're preparing a small SDK patch that does two things: 1) improved streaming buffering with automatic tail-retrieval, and 2) deterministic function-call retries with idempotency tokens surfaced in the user API. Priya, you want to walk through details?
[02:06] Priya Kapoor: Sure. For streaming, we added a 'stream-reassemble' step: when chunks end in the middle of a structural token we hold for up to 2s to allow reassembly; if the connection drops we transparently re-open a short resume call to fetch the remaining bytes. That fixes the common case of jitter. For JSON-schemas we also added a tolerant parser mode that will return the last stable object boundary and a small 'is_truncated' flag, so your validator can either request the remainder or fail gracefully.
[02:39] Alicia Gomez: The tolerant mode sounds useful but we need deterministic failures for auditing. Is there a way we can guarantee either full object or explicit failure with a clear code?
[02:48] Priya Kapoor: Yes — the SDK exposes two modes: strict (fail on any partial) and graceful (return last object + is_truncated). We'll ship both and you can pick per-route.
[02:57] Olivia Chen: About retries, do you support server-side confirmation of function-call execution? We currently rely on the JSON callback to our webhook to mark a tool as executed. If the webhook never arrives but model finished, we get stuck.
[03:09] Priya Kapoor: We do. Our runtime will emit a call-executed event with an execution_id; the SDK will store pending executions keyed by idempotency tokens. On resume, SDK can reconcile against a status endpoint or subscribe to the call-executed stream. The patch will add a local persistence layer for these pending records.
[03:29] Marcus Lee: Any risks with high throughput? We worry about local state explosion on thousands of concurrent user sessions.
[03:36] Priya Kapoor: The local persistence is bounded LRU with configurable TTL — default 10 minutes. For high QPS use you can offload pending state to your own cache (Redis) with the same idempotency token mapping; the SDK includes optional adapters.
[03:50] Jordan Miller: Quick question from Evan — security implication of persisting execution IDs locally. Evan, you on?
[03:56] Evan Roberts: Yeah. We need to ensure those IDs and any payload cached locally aren't exposing PII. Also KMS integration — what encryption at rest and rotation guarantees?
[04:06] Priya Kapoor: Good call. The SDK persistence encrypts with a customer-managed key if you pass in a KMS interface; otherwise it uses an ephemeral key with AES-256. For the hosted flow, we support envelope encryption with your KMS/HSM via our private deploy or dedicated options. We'll include a short security note on this patch.
[04:24] Samira Khan: On the fallback model — you mentioned pinning a fallback variant to "redwood-medium" in the earlier email. What's the expected tradeoff? Latency vs cost vs fidelity?
[04:33] Jordan Miller: Redwood-medium is a lower-cost variant with slightly higher latency tail in some workloads but better deterministic output in tool-calling modes. The tradeoff is lower unit cost and more stable function-call semantics; if you care about highest request fidelity, keep the primary model pinned but configure an automatic fallback to medium only on certain SLO triggers (like >500ms or stream error).
[04:54] Marcus Lee: For the canary we want to limit the blast radius. Can we do route-level pinning for only the reconciliation flows?
[05:00] Priya Kapoor: Yes, you can pin per-route in the console or via API. We'll propose a canary config: 5% of reconciliation traffic, 48h, with automatic rollback on error rate > 0.1%.
[05:11] Alicia Gomez: During the pilot we saw one edge where streaming resumed with a duplicated token causing two sequential function-invokes. Is dedup across resume attempts handled?
[05:20] Priya Kapoor: The deterministic retry uses execution_id + idempotency token to dedupe on the server. If the resume results in duplicate chunks you'll still get the same execution_id and the server will ignore duplicate call attempts. The SDK will also dedupe locally to avoid spamming the network.
[05:35] Olivia Chen: One practical ask: can you give us a small validation harness to run against our staging so we can surface these truncated-object cases?
[05:42] Jordan Miller: Yes, Priya has a harness. Priya?
[05:45] Priya Kapoor: I'll send a harness (small node/python script) that will replay the last 10k sample payloads with jitter patterns and streaming truncation. It will also include a schema validator that uses the SDK tolerant parser and reports failures and truncated boundaries.
[05:59] Samira Khan: Great. On the SSO/SSO audit side, Evan asked about SOC2 scope for the private deploy. Evan, any specific items you want to call out?
[06:08] Evan Roberts: We need clarity on audit logs retention, user-level RBAC granularity, and support for customer-managed HSM for key rotation. Also want to see the runnable evidence for SOC2 if available.
[06:17] Jordan Miller: We'll attach our SOC2 summary and a dedicated appendix for Private's HSM integration. That can be in the security packet.
[06:23] Marcus Lee: Back to the SDK: will the patch be a major semver bump? We prefer not to break existing behavior in staging.
transcript_continued:
[06:29] Priya Kapoor: It's a minor bump; default behavior preserves current APIs. You opt into the new restart/resume and idempotency via a new config flag. We'll document migration steps.
[06:38] Olivia Chen: Anything else on metrics and observability? We want token-level latency and per-tool cost breakdown to map to vendor payouts.
[06:45] Jordan Miller: Console can expose token-level and per-route cost; for pilot customers we can share a CSV export. For the canary we'll give you a dashboard with traces and the call-executed event stream.
[06:56] Alicia Gomez: Quick note — we saw a few long tail latencies on large context windows when KV cache misses combined with bursty traffic. Could that cause more truncated streams?
[07:07] Priya Kapoor: Possibly. If the runtime hits a slow path it's more likely you'll see chunk boundary jitter. Our recommendation: enable prefix caching for reconciliation flows and reduce max concurrent sequences per session. We'll share batching config suggestions.
[07:21] Samira Khan: Ok, recap of decisions?
[07:24] Jordan Miller: Recap: Redwood sends SDK patch + harness; customer runs 48h canary pinned to fallback model for reconciliation flows; customer runs validation harness and shares results; Redwood shares SOC2/security appendix and KMS/HSM integration doc. Action items in the notes.
[07:40] Alicia Gomez: Sounds good. Any blockers for start?
[07:43] Jordan Miller: None from our side — we'll aim to send artifacts by Fri.
[07:47] Evan Roberts: I'll follow up separately on a list of regulatory questions.
[07:50] Priya Kapoor: One more quick technical note — if you want strong-at-most-once semantics for tool-calls, you need an external ledger/commit after execution; we can help design that pattern but it's outside the SDK's default guarantees.
[08:02] Marcus Lee: Good to know. We'll discuss with our backend team.
[08:06] Jordan Miller: Thanks everyone, we'll send the notes and schedule the canary kickoff for Wednesday next week.
[08:12] Meeting end.
notes: SDK patch will include stream reassembly + tolerant parser + deterministic retry
Validation harness to reproduce streaming truncation patterns (node/python)
Canary: route-level pin to fallback model (redwood-medium), 5% traffic, 48h, automatic rollback on >0.1% error rate
